headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and use MCP/broad egress, while Argo Workflows can move artifacts and parameters through workflow outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists if Argo Workflows materializes attacker-controlled artifacts or parameters that Semantic Kernel later ingests as trusted content. Semantic Kernel explicitly supports MCP servers and plugin/function calling, so untrusted content could steer tool use; Argo’s workflow outputs can carry raw data. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Argo workflow outputs are copied into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs without sanitization
IF an MCP plugin or OpenAPI tool in Semantic Kernel parses workflow-produced text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and schema check before passing Argo outputs into Semantic Kernel
Disable MCP plugins for any workflow step that consumes untrusted text
Require a human review step for prompt-bearing artifacts
Log and reject inputs containing tool directives or role-like markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workflow artifacts and agent inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel can read files and has broad network egress to third-party model providers; Argo Workflows handles artifacts and parameters. If shared files or artifacts contain sensitive data, Semantic Kernel may transmit them to external inference backends. Argo itself is not shown to exfiltrate, but the pair creates a default path from shared workspace data into outbound model calls.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or artifact directory
IF Semantic Kernel sends file contents or context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face
mitigations: Restrict Semantic Kernel to a redacted input directory
Move secrets and parameters out of shared artifacts
Turn off outbound model calls for sensitive runs
Review and minimize files mounted into the kernel process
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can orchestrate artifacts and parameters, while Semantic Kernel can write files and use MCP tools against plugins. Even without explicit git or shell access, both can mutate shared application-defined files or state, creating write contention and inconsistent outputs. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the overlap is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined directory or artifact store
IF an MCP plugin mutates shared state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator step
Make shared files read-only for one agent
Check timestamps before overwriting artifacts
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel can treat upstream content as plugin input, and Argo Workflows can propagate parameters and artifacts downstream. If Argo-produced outputs are consumed by Semantic Kernel without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect tool calls or generated actions. There is no cited verification layer in either profile, so the interaction is plausible in default orchestration patterns.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are fed directly into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin arguments
IF Semantic Kernel acts on those inputs without a validation step
mitigations: Insert a validation step between workflow output and agent input
Require structured JSON with schema validation
Have a second agent or rule-based checker verify critical fields
Block automatic execution on low-confidence outputs
requires-engineering: add end-to-end approval gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a concrete compliance breach is not proven. However, Semantic Kernel’s broad egress and secret handling plus Argo’s artifact/parameter handling create a small compliance gap if regulated data is routed through external model providers. The evidence is indirect, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin calls
IF the external model provider is outside the required residency or DPA boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of model prompts
Use a residency-approved provider only
Redact identifiers before workflow handoff
Review retention settings for model providers
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements
